output.text:
I made a one-line fix in `src/slug.js`. I haven't run the tests: the `npm test` call needed approval and wasn't run.

**The bug:** at `src/slug.js:14`, the regex that trims separators from the ends was missing the global (`g`) flag:

```js
.replace(new RegExp(`^${sep}|${sep}$`), '')
```

Without `g`, `.replace` only removes the first match. When a title has punctuation or spaces at both ends, only the leading separator was stripped. For example, `'  Hello, World!  '` became `'-hello-world-'` and then `'hello-world-'`. That breaks the `drops punctuation at both ends` unit test. It would also fail the property tests that check slug format and idempotence.

**The fix:**

```js
.replace(new RegExp(`^${sep}|${sep}$`, 'g'), '')
```

I also read through the truncation logic and the other tests and didn't find anything else that should fail. To check the fix, run:

```
npm install
npm test
```

(`npm install` is needed first if `fast-check` isn't installed; I didn't see a `node_modules` folder.)
